messages:
jamal: Heads-up: our CI started failing on `poetry lock` during the SDK install step. It stalls in resolver and times out. CI is Ubuntu 22.04, poetry 1.4.2 in the image. Anyone seen a similar pattern?
hana: We saw a similar issue last month with a transitive dependency pulling in old backports. Which SDK version?
jamal: redwood-sdk==0.12.1 (we upgraded last week). Locally `pip install` works fine but `poetry lock` takes forever then OOM on CI runner.
owen: Could be a many-combination solver explosion. Does the package publish both wheel and sdist? Poetry consults package metadata differently than pip.
jamal: PyPI has a manylinux wheel and a sdist. The wheel METADATA looks normal. I captured resolver logs with `poetry -vvv lock` and it's repeatedly trying different markers.
lucy: Any platform markers or extras like `asyncio`/`http2`? Those often cause extra optional deps.
jamal: extras: "http2", "torch", "docs". No platform-specific markers.
hana: Two quick customer-facing mitigations: (1) switch CI to use `pip` to install wheel into the venv before running poetry (hacky but effective), (2) pin a small set of common transitive deps in pyproject to reduce resolve space (typing-extensions, httpx).
owen: Another angle: generate a constraints file from a working env and pass `--constraints` to pip; for poetry you can try `poetry lock --no-update --skip-optional` but that flag isn't ideal.
jamal: I tried `poetry lock --no-update` and `poetry lock -n` both hang. `poetry env use 3.10` didn't change it. Upgrading Poetry to 1.5.3 in CI reduced the time but didn't eliminate spikes.
lucy: We added a small repro that multiplies packages and shows combinatorial blow up. I'll attach profiler output. Also note: our monorepo already pins typing-extensions to ^4.6 which helps.
hana: Could SDK looseness be at fault? If redwood-sdk's dependent ranges are too permissive (e.g., `httpx>=0.23` rather than a bounded range) the resolver experiments more versions. Can we ask SDK team to tighten some ranges or publish an extra wheel tag?
owen: For packaging side, we can ensure wheels on PyPI include proper Requires-Dist entries instead of relying on environment markers. Also consider adding a minimal `pyproject` with pinned build-system deps to sdist.
jamal: Temporary fix applied: added `typing-extensions = "^4.6"` to our pyproject and upgraded CI poetry to 1.5.3. Lockfile completes reliably now. But this is not ideal for customers on older poetry.
lucy: Action items: (1) DevEx doc with recommended workarounds (pin common transitive deps, upgrade poetry, pip fallback), (2) SDK to run a CI job that runs `poetry lock` in a minimal project to catch resolver churn, (3) consider a release that narrows some ranges or provides a `redwood-sdk[core]` minimal extra.
hana: I'll draft the doc. Owen, can you open an SDK issue with repro and attach the `-vvv` resolver trace?
owen: Done: INFRA-8470 created, assignee eng-runtime. Included repro steps, `poetry -vvv lock` output, and suggested change: bound httpx to `<0.25` in the next release.
jamal: Small note for support desk: if customers hit this, recommend `pip install redwood-sdk==<version>` to get a wheel, or pin `typing-extensions` and upgrade poetry.
pip-bot: Ticket INFRA-8470 created by owen; severity: medium; labels: packaging, poetry, sdk.
lucy: Also adding an internal test that runs `poetry lock` with latest poetry versions (1.4.x and 1.5.x) as part of the SDK release pipeline. That should catch regressions.
jamal: Thanks all. Keeping the thread open until SDK PR lands.
